v1.prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Create a NEW six-panel sequential comic, arranged three columns by two rows, landscape overall, read left to right top row then bottom row. The supplied image is an ORIGINAL CHARACTER AND MATERIAL REFERENCE from our own prior work, not a target whose panel story should be copied. Keep the same middle-aged short wavy dark-haired woman in a worn blue-green work coat and the same lean weathered middle-aged man with messy brown hair, long nose and an ochre work shirt. Keep their unglamorous expressive faces, dry graphite/woodcut hatching, opaque gouache on rough tan paper, chipped ink panel borders, restricted teal/ochre/dusty mauve palette. Same small dockside sail repair workshop at dusk. This is a subtle story about where one puts the light, not a magical transformation. There is ONE repaired oil lantern in the story and ONE intact folded paper bird mask, recognizable long beak and angular eye holes, now mounted on a short wooden display peg; nobody wears it. The lantern is the only strong local warm work light. Six panels exactly: 1 Wide workshop establishing view: man at left bench proudly admires his paper bird mask on its display peg, with the sole lit lantern placed immediately in front of the mask, spotlighting it. At a separate right bench farther away, the woman is working independently on a visibly torn off-white sail, her hands and seam in deep blue dusk shadow. Show both benches and the physical distance. 2 Closer on woman threading a needle and trying to see the torn sail seam in the poor light, eyes open, focused and capable rather than helpless; in foreground edge the man has turned to notice her hands. 3 Medium shot: the man deliberately LIFTS the lit lantern by its top handle away from the display peg; the paper bird mask stays intact on that same peg but falls into cool shadow. His arm and the lantern are fully visible with convincing grip, not fused with the mask. 4 Medium wide at the woman's work bench: he SETS the same lantern onto the clear space beside her torn sail; warm light now visibly reaches her hands and fabric. She looks up to meet his open eyes while keeping one hand on her work. 5 Close shared work: woman actually guides needle and thread across the sail seam while man holds the separated cloth edges together; their hands have different clear tasks, lantern stands beside the seam, not held by either person, no embraces. 6 Wide from substantially the SAME CAMERA POSITION as panel 1: both people at the right bench concentrating together on the sail in the warm pool from that same lantern; the left display peg and paper bird mask remain clearly visible but unlit in cool shadow. The man's change is visible through his choice and its practical consequence; the mask has NOT disappeared or been destroyed. No dialogue, captions, numbers, written words, speech balloons, modern technology, extra lanterns, extra characters or extra mask. Preserve tactile dry paper texture throughout; avoid glossy 3D, photorealism, cute cartoon, smooth digital airbrush or sentimental smiling poses.
